engagement_title: OSTRA, one room across two services: a low light plate set that survives both a near black site and a white delivery card, plus the per cover menu run the old printer took with him
vertical: Food, restaurant and beverage, contemporary seasonal tasting counter, twenty two seats, coastal New England
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork post quoted in this ledger row's grounding_note, from a boutique digital studio commissioning a premium restaurant website described as high end, clean, modern minimalist, with a Dark Mode aesthetic that focuses heavily on high quality food photography, across Home, an interactive food menu and Booking, mobile responsive. The real post names no restaurant, so the room is laundered to the coined OSTRA and the client stays an unnamed studio whose own front end developer builds the site. The web build itself is out of connector scope, and the ledger's verdict is that what remained sat on one surface. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller commission is: the studio's designer needs finished photographs rather than raw files, the same plates have to survive a delivery platform's white card as well as the room's near black page, a client supplied press PDF now converts into a live merge template so the per cover menu card the room prints nightly becomes real record per page work, and HTML authoring produces a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes for the entry screens and the booking graphic. So this is the photographer's half of that website job as the room actually needed it bought.
client_one_liner: Our plates were shot across two services and read as two different evenings, the delivery platforms put them on a white card next to everybody else, and we hand write the menu cards because the printer who set them up is gone.
client_brief:
OSTRA. Twenty two seats around the pass, one seasonal tasting menu at a hundred and thirty five dollars a head, four nights a week.

We are rebuilding the site with a small studio and their designer needs finished photographs from us rather than raw files. The site is dark: near black, very little on the page, one plate at a time. That is the room, so that is the site.

The pictures were shot across two services by a friend who cooks with us. First service ran early and second service ran late, and the pass lighting at nine is not the pass lighting at six. Looked at one at a time they are lovely. Scrolled one after another they are obviously two different evenings. We need them to read as one set: one temperature, one depth of shadow, gloss that still looks like gloss rather than a grey patch.

We also list on two delivery platforms for the Sunday supper box. Those platforms put every picture on a white card in a grid next to everybody else's, and ours currently vanish there.

Then the printed menu. Every guest gets a card at their seat with their name, the date, the courses and their pairing flight. Our old printer set that up and we lost him. We print about forty a night, we want to run tonight's covers ourselves each afternoon, and we want to see proofs before anything prints.

Last, the two screens in the entry and a square graphic for booking confirmations. Those are ours to design and they should feel like walking into the room rather than like an advertisement.

A hundred and thirty five dollars, guests thirty to fifty five, booking an occasion six weeks out. Quiet, dark, unhurried. Not a bistro and not a hotel restaurant. Tell us what you did to each plate and why that plate needed something different.
price_band_and_audience: A 135 dollar seasonal tasting counter, guests 30 to 55 booking six weeks ahead for an occasion. The band is load bearing and it dictates a specific grammar: a near black ground, one plate per frame, generous emptiness, restrained saturation, and speculars on sauce and glass that still read as light rather than as blown white or flattened grey. That restraint is what a guest is paying for and what makes a six week wait feel reasonable. Grade the same plates bright, warm, saturated and crowded, with two dishes per frame and a garnish filling every corner, and the room reads as a 14 dollar plate at a busy bistro, which at this cheque size does not read as friendly, it reads as a mistake the guest is about to make. Push the other way into near monochrome art photography with the food unreadable and it becomes a gallery rather than a dinner, and a guest cannot tell what they are booking. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 1,400 to 3,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.about: OSTRA is a counter, not a dining room: guests sit around the pass for one seasonal tasting menu at 135 dollars a head. The room is near black, spare and unhurried, and the photography is meant to feel like walking into it rather than like an advertisement. One plate at a time, on a dark ground, with light that still reads as light.
brand_identity.audience: Guests aged 30 to 55 booking an occasion around six weeks ahead, who expect calm and consideration rather than volume.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A 135 dollar seasonal tasting counter. The grammar is a near black ground, one plate per frame, generous emptiness, restrained saturation, and speculars on sauce and glass that read as light rather than as blown white or flat grey. Never a bright, crowded bistro look, and never near monochrome art photography in which the food cannot be read.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet editorial serif for course titles and guest names paired with a minimal sans for detail lines, set light on a near black ground. Spare and considered, neither bistro chalkboard nor hotel gilt.
brand_identity.voice: Spare and understated, the voice of a room that lets the plate speak. Example line the brand would write: "Five courses. One seating. Please arrive as the light goes."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There are no editable brand files. The per guest menu card survives only as the old printer's press PDF, and the printer has been lost, so the room hand writes about forty cards a night. A dark mode site reference screengrab was supplied as mood only, and course titles come spelled as the kitchen spells them.
brand_identity.values: Honesty of the room and one plate at a time: the photographs are this kitchen's real plates, and restraint is what the guest is paying for.

assets_supplied.name: ostra_service_one/ (7 plates, 5472 x 3648)
assets_supplied.kind: First service captures shot on the near black slate pass, one plate per frame, available pass light with a grey reference card held in the opening frame.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "First service. The card is in the very first frame if that helps."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The pass lighting was switched from its early setting to its evening setting partway through this service, so the folder is not one illuminant, and the reference card was shot before the switch, which means grading the whole folder to the card takes the later four frames green and cool. Two of the seven are also plated on a dark rimmed dish whose rim runs close to the slate in value on the shadow side.

assets_supplied.name: ostra_service_two/ (6 plates)
assets_supplied.kind: Second service captures on the same pass, later in the evening, no reference card in any frame.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Second service, later, warmer. No card, we forgot."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two frames carry speculars that were already clipped in the capture, a glossy reduction on one plate and a coupe glass on another, so a highlight recovery move on those frames succeeds and changes nothing at all. One of the six is also the same dish as a service one frame, plated differently for a menu change, which nothing in the filenames or the course list distinguishes.

assets_supplied.name: ostra_menu_card_autumn.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The old printer's press PDF of last season's per guest menu card, A5 portrait, printed from the printer's layout with font subsets embedded: a guest line, a date line, a five course list and a pairing block.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Last season's card as the printer made it. He set it up, we lost him, and nobody here can edit it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The frame carrying the guest line, the course list and the pairing block is a fixed measure frame set to last season's shorter dish names, and text that runs past its depth does not spill or error, it simply stops rendering at the frame edge while the page still exports and the page count stays correct. The conversion also exposes the whole card as a single continuous flow rather than the four blocks the printed page shows.

assets_supplied.name: ostra_covers.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Tonight's covers: guest name, party size, date, seat, course list variant and pairing flight, roughly forty rows.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Tonight as the book has it. This is what we would key in every afternoon."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Several records carry a hyphenated double surname together with a dietary variant line, which makes them materially longer than the rest of the run, and two records have an empty pairing cell because those guests are not drinking, which merges as a blank line rather than closing up.

assets_supplied.name: ostra_room_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the room's own words about the look, the course titles as the kitchen writes them, and the studio designer's stated need for finished files rather than raw.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "How we talk about the room, and the course names spelled the way the kitchen spells them."

assets_supplied.name: ostra_house_mark_plate.jpg (single frame)
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of OSTRA's house mark as it survives in the room: the wordmark and a small incised oyster shell device blind engraved into a subdued brass plate mounted at the end of the pass, shot at a raking angle under the room's single tungsten source so the engraving reads as relief rather than as ink.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only version of the mark. It is cut into a brass plate at the end of the pass, there is no file anywhere, and it is the wordmark plus the little shell."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The mark carries no ink at all: it is blind engraving read only as a thin bright edge and a shadow in each incised stroke, so a selection naming the plate or the brass returns the substrate and a selection naming a dark mark on a light ground finds nothing, and across the shadowed half of the plate the engraved strokes and the brass run close in value. It is a compound lockup, so a selection naming the whole mark returns the wordmark and silently drops the small oyster device, and the hairline serifs and the fine incised shell lines hold at full canvas but close into solid strokes at the height the mark actually reproduces at the top of the near black page and foil sized on the menu card.

assets_supplied.name: ostra_reference_darksite.png
assets_supplied.kind: Screengrab of a dark mode restaurant site the owners like, supplied as a proportion and mood reference.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Roughly the feeling. We are not asking you to copy it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The screengrab is a three times retina phone capture, so its pixel dimensions are device pixels and not layout points: the wordmark measured off it and matched one to one lands the recovered mark well below the height at which its serifs hold on the near black ground. And the proportion it demonstrates is a single portrait phone frame, so the plate to ground ratio it shows cannot be lifted directly onto the wide hero or the square booking graphic, whose grammar has to be re-derived rather than the ratio copied.

acceptance_bar: All thirteen plates read as ONE set when scrolled one after another: one temperature, one depth of shadow, one distance from the plate. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named in the note, not shipped at eighty percent.
Gloss still reads as gloss. No specular on sauce, glaze or glassware is delivered as a flat white patch or as a flattened grey patch, and no plate rim is lost into the near black ground.
The delivery tiles read correctly on a white card in a grid beside other restaurants, not only on our own black page. A tile that is beautiful on black and muddy on white fails.
No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no crop tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry. No plate edge is invented to reach a wider aspect.
The menu run produces one card per cover in book order, and every record is complete at trim: the longest names and the dietary variants are fully present on the printed page.
No card carries a stranded blank line where a guest has no pairing.
Every course title is spelled as the kitchen spells it, on every card.

The entry screens, the wide hero and the booking square sit in ONE working file, each keeping its own canvas size, with live editable text and every photograph carried as embedded image data, delivered with the self contained source.

On every collateral canvas the plate reads as sitting in the room's darkness rather than as a bright rectangle pasted onto a black panel, and that holds on the canvases beyond the first as well as on the first.
One type system across all three canvases, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used.
The note states, per plate, what was applied and why that plate needed something its neighbours did not, plus every resize any tool reported and every frame that could not be brought to the set.

The house mark is delivered as placeable vector artwork rather than a photograph of the brass plate: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, the incised oyster device present alongside the wordmark, and every serif and shell line still open at the height the mark actually reproduces at the top of the near black page and foil sized on the menu card, on the near black ground rather than on white, with a stated safe minimum height.

On the entry screens the plate to ground proportion and the wordmark's placement and scale follow the grammar of the supplied dark site reference rather than being invented, and the recovered mark is never set below its safe minimum height even where the reference's own retina shrunk apparent scale would put it there.

adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_adjust_color_temperature, image_adjust_highlights, image_adjust_light_portions, image_adjust_dark_portions, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_invert_selection, image_apply_preset, image_remove_background (transparent and backgroundColor routes), image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor), image_vectorize (no options, all tuning in the raster preparation)
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision in the commission. It sets one low light target and brings two services and two pass lighting settings to it one call at a time, protects speculars per plate because a recovery that suits a matte plate glares on a glazed one, produces the second grade the white delivery card needs from the same masters, cuts the plate free of the slate for the platform tiles, and crops each destination downscale only without inventing a plate edge to reach a wider aspect. It also recovers the room's house mark from the brass plate at engraving level, wording the selection to the incised strokes rather than to the plate and taking the small oyster device on its own, then performs the vector hygiene the optionless tracer does not, injecting a viewBox and removing the opaque full canvas ground path so the mark is placeable rather than a picture of a plate.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (as readout and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (recordRange, one press PDF branch), document_render_layout (resolution, pageRange, createSeparateFiles)
adobe_surfaces.role: The nightly per cover menu card. The old printer's press PDF is reverse engineered into a live merge template, tonight's book drives one card per cover at true trim, and the run is delivered both as a press PDF in book order and as proofs rendered at real resolution, which is the only place a merged record's behaviour at trim can actually be read.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The two entry screens, the wide hero panel and the square booking graphic as one native editable document carrying roots at their own canvas sizes, the only surface in the connector that composes free form fixed canvas layout. Every plate must be pulled down and inlined as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, family and weight are declared on every text element, and the whole dark mode look depends on how the importer normalises the way a plate is joined to its ground.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system for the collateral canvases and the written specification the studio's designer will build the site's own CSS against. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's art direction and has to land on quiet and unhurried rather than on either bistro chalkboard or hotel gilt. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form before the kit call because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or it falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one frame the room does not own, a low light interior texture band for the wide entry hero, IP clean and at genuine camera scale with generative tech candidates excluded, and graded to the same low light target so it does not read as bought from a different restaurant. The Boards half persists the selects the owners and the studio's designer sign off from, placed within the twelve per call cap, with a 201 read as partial success.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: The plates are raster work for someone else's build, the menu cards are a record per page run that only the layout surface does, and the entry and booking pieces need an authored fixed canvas document. The web build itself is explicitly the studio's and is not attempted here.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: The manifest is keyed by course rather than by filename, because the two folders overlap on one dish and the filenames do not say so.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by course and service.

trajectory.action: Preview all thirteen plates and triage them: which service, which illuminant within that service, which are canted, which carry gloss, which plate rims run close to the slate, and which dishes are actually the same dish.
trajectory.judgement: The room asserts two services. The pictures are the only place that can be settled, and reading the frames against the course list is slower than counting files and is not the same thing.
trajectory.produces: A per plate triage note covering illuminant, tilt, gloss, rim separation and course identity.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is canted before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the plate and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop, and at this band a tilted horizon on the pass reads as carelessness rather than as style.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Render one plate two ways, a cooler near monochrome low light and a warmer candlelit low light, argue one against the band and the room's own words, then fix that target and correct each of the thirteen toward it with its own call.
trajectory.judgement: The reference card is evidence about the moment it was shot in, not about the folder it sits in, and one batched call applies one identical parameter set across two services and two pass settings. The choice between the two directions is taste, and a hundred and thirty five dollar counter is not a candlelit bistro.
trajectory.produces: A defended low light target and thirteen corrected masters at source scale with a per plate parameter log.

trajectory.action: Work the highlights and the darks per plate so gloss still reads as light and the plate rim still separates from the slate, then look at each result rather than at the response.
trajectory.judgement: One highlight setting cannot serve a glazed reduction and a matte terrine at once, and one shadow setting cannot serve a dark rimmed dish and a pale one. The move that protects a specular on one plate flattens a rim on the next.
trajectory.produces: Thirteen plates whose gloss and shadow behaviour has been judged individually against the one target.

trajectory.action: Derive the second grade the delivery platforms need, judging every candidate tile on a white card in a grid rather than on the room's black page.
trajectory.judgement: The grade that carries the site is a decision made for a near black ground, and the platform's white card inverts the contrast argument entirely. Two grades from one master is the answer; one grade stretched across both destinations is the failure.
trajectory.produces: A second graded family for the platform tiles, judged in the context it will actually appear in.

trajectory.action: Cut the plates free of the slate for the platform tiles and cut every destination crop, downscale only, reading every returned tradeoff rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: The platform grid puts a plate beside a competitor's, so the plate has to hold its own edge on white. The wider screen aspect cannot be reached by inventing plate or slate that was never photographed, so the answer is a tighter crop or a different frame.
trajectory.produces: Platform ready plate cutouts and the destination crop set, each with its tradeoffs recorded.

trajectory.action: Recover the room's house mark from the brass plate: an ink level selection worded to the engraved strokes' own thin bright edge and shadow rather than to the plate, the correct polarity for a mark that is relief and not ink, a bounds crop driven by the selection's own returned box, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed, and a first look at the result set small on the near black ground it will actually sit on.
trajectory.judgement: Three things the tools will not decide: how to word a selection for a mark that carries no ink at all so it takes the engraving and not the brass, that a selection naming the whole lockup returns the wordmark and silently drops the small oyster device so the device has to be taken on its own, and that image_vectorize accepts no options at all so every lever that governs whether the serifs and the shell lines survive lives in the raster preparation before the trace and not in the trace call.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent house mark with a real viewBox and no opaque ground path, delivered as a Bone reversing version for the near black ground and a Subdued Brass colour accurate variant, with the oyster device present alongside the wordmark.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for a low light interior texture band for the entry hero, filter to photography, exclude generative tech results, license and download at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the low light target, not the prettiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale frame graded into the same darkness.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's, judged against a quiet, unhurried, occasion booking room rather than against a bistro or a hotel dining room. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role, written down for the studio's developer.

trajectory.action: Convert the menu card PDF, export the IDML, and read the real frame inventory: how many frames exist, what each story truly contains, and how deep the frame carrying the course list actually is.
trajectory.judgement: Frame granularity from a PDF is not under anyone's control and the printed card is not evidence of it. Promising a per block mapping before looking is how a nightly run ships half populated.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory naming every mappable target and the true depth and measure of the frame the courses live in.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct the true story text from the IDML story runs, compute every offset from that string, build and validate the mapping, prepare the template, then round trip the IDML and confirm by inspection that every placeholder is present.
trajectory.judgement: The structure readout and the validator both speak with confidence and neither of them reads the document. The only evidence a placeholder exists is finding it in the story after preparation.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory has been read back from the document rather than reported.

trajectory.action: Merge tonight's book to one press PDF in book order and render proofs at true resolution, then read the actual printed pages, choosing the longest names, the dietary variants and the two records with no pairing rather than the first three pages.
trajectory.judgement: A forty record run is checked by choosing the records most likely to break, not by sampling the top of the file. Page count matching row count says nothing about what is on any page.
trajectory.produces: A press PDF of tonight's covers and a proof set whose worst case records have actually been read.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML with roots at their own canvas sizes for the two entry screens, the wide hero and the booking square, inline every plate as image data, declare family and weight on every text element, and build the join between plate and ground that the whole dark mode look rests on, then upload the file and hold the returned URL. Place the recovered house mark as inline vector at the top of the entry screens and at the head of the booking square, sized and positioned from the dark site reference's grammar rather than from its retina shrunk apparent dimensions.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how much darkness the page is allowed to keep at this band. The reference is proportion evidence and not a measuring stick: its apparent wordmark scale is in device pixels, and matched literally it sets the mark below the height its serifs survive.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the whole collateral set, retained as the durable source deliverable. The recovered mark is carried as live vector rather than a flattened picture.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per canvas markup for every other canvas. And confirm from that same markup that the placed mark is live vector geometry, not a raster, at or above its safe minimum height on every canvas.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at page one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a per canvas markup audit for the rest. The recovered mark is confirmed to have carried across as vector and to hold at reproduction size.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board, add both graded families and the licensed frame within the per call placement cap, re-send only the entries the response names as failed, then write the handover note for the owners and the studio's designer.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success. The note has two readers with different needs: the room needs to know what to reshoot, the developer needs the type system and which grade goes on which ground.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: That on two of the second service frames the highlight move does nothing at all. The gloss on those speculars was already clipped in the capture, so there is no information left in that range to recover: the call returns ordinary success, the parameters are accepted, and the result is visually identical to the input in exactly the region the whole low light grammar depends on. The readout is that nothing moved. Whether a given specular still holds detail is a property of that individual exposure and is not visible from the frame at preview scale, nor stated by any tool, nor distinguishable from a highlight move that simply had a small effect.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it, because the only way to learn whether a range still carries information is to move it and look; doing it right first time would mean knowing which two of thirteen exposures were clipped before touching them. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks that gloss still look like gloss, which is the room's art direction, not a disclosure that two captures are already blown. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the answer is a different treatment for those frames, bringing the whole exposure down so the specular sits back inside the range and lifting the darks to hold the plate, or conceding the frame and naming it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan those two plates from the master rather than from the corrected file, re-expose them so the specular re-enters the range and rebuild the shadow end underneath, re-judge them against the other eleven in a strip, and if the frame still cannot join the set say so in the note rather than shipping it at eighty percent and letting it define the hero.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A hero plate and a course tile whose sauce is a flat white shape and whose glassware has no edge, published as the first thing a guest sees on a dark page at a cheque size where gloss is most of the promise.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: That the card's text frame does not spill, it stops. The frame was set to last season's shorter course titles, and the records carrying a hyphenated double surname together with a dietary variant line run past its depth. There is no overflow, no error and no warning: the page exports, the page count still equals the row count, and the record is simply cut off at the frame edge with the pairing block missing. Which records do it depends on the interaction between this season's course titles and this particular book of covers, and the effect is invisible in every response and in the page count, appearing only on the rendered page of the specific records that overrun.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it: the frame's real depth is a property of the printer's original document and the overrun is a property of tonight's data, so it exists only once the two are merged and rendered. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the card carries the guest, the date, the courses and the pairing, and the acceptance requirement that every record be complete at trim is the client's standing demand, not a warning that a frame truncates. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response changes the template or the copy fitting rules, not the merge arguments.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Identify which records overrun by reading the rendered pages of the longest and most awkward records rather than the first few, then change the thing that actually fits: the frame's measure or depth in the template, or the course line breaking, or the treatment of the dietary variant, re-prepare, re-merge and re-render, and re-read those same worst case records plus the two with an empty pairing cell.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Forty cards printed and laid at forty seats, of which several are missing the guest's pairing flight or half their surname, on the one object every guest touches at a hundred and thirty five dollars a head.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark is still the mark at the height it actually reproduces. The trace comes back looking correct: the wordmark is there, the oyster device is there, the counters and the incised shell lines are open, and at full canvas on a light page it is a faithful recovery. But the mark sits small at the top of the near black entry screen and foil sized at the head of the menu card, and at that height on a near black ground the hairline serifs and the fine shell lines fill in and the small counters close into solid strokes. image_vectorize takes no options at all, so nothing about the trace call can be tuned; the only evidence is placing the artwork at its real reproduction size on the near black ground and looking, and the near black ground is exactly where it is least forgiving.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the answer depends on the trace, the reproduction height and the near black ground being present together, and the first two are produced by the agent while the third is a property of the room's own site. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for a mark that still reads as the room's, and the acceptance line that every serif hold at reproduction height is the room's own art direction, not a warning. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a different raster preparation feeding the same optionless tracer, a differently worded selection, a fill and flatten plate instead of a binary mask, or a bounds crop that changes what the tracer sees, since the tracer itself carries no lever.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-prepare the raster on a different route, re-trace, re-inject the viewBox and strip the opaque ground path again, then re-place the mark at reproduction height on the near black ground and re-judge. Once a safe minimum height is actually known, raise the wordmark on the entry screens to respect it even though the supplied dark site reference's own retina shrunk apparent scale would set it smaller, which sends the placement back through the Express authoring step rather than leaving it where the reference implied.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The first thing a guest sees on the near black page is the room's name reduced to a row of solid blobs with the oyster device gone, and the same mark foil sized on the one object every guest touches at the seat, discovered on the glass and on the card rather than in the file.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the join between the plate and the room's darkness, which is the entire dark mode look. Authored the natural way, that join is a blended overlay panel and a softly translucent booking panel over the hero; the importer drops blend behaviour outright and renders the element as a plain opaque shape, and it drops the translucency treatment and keeps only the underlying flat fill, both at full success with no warning of any kind. The returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports it, and the document's own rendition returns the first artboard only, so the second entry screen and the booking square can be checked no other way. Whether what survives still reads as a plate sitting in darkness, or as a bright rectangle behind an opaque grey slab, is visible only after the export.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step; and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks that the pieces feel like walking into the room, and the acceptance line about a plate sitting in darkness is the room's own art direction, not a warning. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the answer is a different upstream asset, a plate whose fall to darkness is baked into the raster before it ever reaches the layout, or a construction built only from what the importer demonstrably keeps.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the affected plates so the transition to the ground exists in the image itself rather than in the page, or re-author the canvases using only constructions the returned markup shows surviving, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit every canvas from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: An editable collateral set handed to the studio in which the booking square and the second entry screen show a plate behind an opaque grey panel, with the export having reported success throughout and only the first canvas ever having been looked at.

deliverables.spec: Thirteen plates from two services and two pass lighting settings brought to one defended low light target with one temperature, one shadow depth and gloss that still reads as light, levelled where they were canted, plus one licensed camera scale interior frame graded into the same darkness. Delivered with a per plate parameter log stating what was applied and why that plate needed something its neighbours did not, and naming any frame that could not join the set. This is one set with one target, not thirteen separately pleasing pictures.

deliverables.name: Delivery platform tile set
deliverables.spec: Per dish square tiles derived from the same masters but graded and cut for a white card in a competitor grid: the plate free of the slate with an edge that holds against white, judged in that context rather than on the room's black page. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions with the returned tradeoff record for each, and no plate edge invented to reach an aspect. Where a quiet maker's mark is set in a tile corner it is the recovered vector mark rather than a shrunk raster logo, and it must still read on the white card at that small size.

deliverables.spec: The room's house mark, the wordmark and its small incised oyster device, recovered from the brass plate as placeable scalable artwork with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, the oyster device present alongside the wordmark, delivered as a single colour Bone reversing version for the near black ground and a Subdued Brass colour accurate variant, holding its serifs and its shell lines at the height it actually sits at the top of the entry screen and foil sized on the menu card, on the near black ground rather than on white, with a stated safe minimum height. This is the mark that carries the wordmark across the site header, the entry screens, the menu card and any tile that sets a maker's mark, not a shrunk raster logo.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster work for someone else's build, which need a record per page run, and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that the web build itself is explicitly not this commission.
Whether the reference card is evidence about its folder or only about the moment it was shot in, and what to grade to when the later half of that folder sits under a different pass setting.
Which of two low light directions to commit to, a cooler near monochrome or a warmer candlelit one, argued against a 135 dollar occasion counter rather than against one attractive frame.
How far to protect a specular per plate, given that the move that saves gloss on a glazed reduction flattens the rim on a dark rimmed dish.
Whether the site grade can serve the delivery platform's white card, or whether two grades from one master is the honest answer.
How to reach a wider screen aspect without inventing plate or slate, which means a tighter crop or a different frame rather than a generated edge.
Whether thirteen files across two folders are thirteen dishes, and how to say so when one dish appears twice.
Which fields of the menu card can be mapped to frames of their own and which have to be reached inside a single flow, decided from the document's real inventory rather than from the printed card.
Which records to actually read in a forty record run, given that page count matching row count is not evidence about any page.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a quiet occasion room, plus the real numeric weight per family and the specification the studio's developer will build from.
How much darkness the collateral is allowed to keep. At this band emptiness is the design, and a bright, busy, garnish filled canvas is a correct looking wrong answer.

How to word the ink level selection so it takes the engraved mark and not the brass plate it is cut into, given the mark carries no ink at all, and how to keep the small oyster device that a selection naming the whole lockup silently drops.

How to read the supplied dark site reference as proportion and placement evidence given it is a retina capture whose apparent wordmark scale, taken at face value, would set the recovered mark below the height at which its serifs and shell lines survive on the near black ground.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns beautiful pictures of food. IDENTITY: these are this kitchen's real plates, plated the way this chef plates them, and a guest who booked six weeks ahead on a generated dish is being sold something the pass cannot serve; the dish that appears twice under two platings is precisely the kind of fact a regenerated set erases. SPEC: the delivery platforms need square tiles that survive a white card in a competitor grid, the entry screens need exact canvases, and none of that is satisfiable or checkable from a generated frame. EDITABILITY: the menu card has to exist as a template the room re-runs every afternoon against a new book of covers, and the collateral has to be editable because the season changes, neither of which a flat render is. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this highlight move do anything at all, did this record print complete at trim, did the darkness survive the import. And the house mark is a specific mark cut into the room's own brass plate that has to be RECOVERED as vector paths rather than reinvented: a regenerated wordmark is a different room's name in a different hand, the site header and the menu card need closed paths that still read at a stated small height on a near black ground, and whether the serifs hold at reproduction size is exactly the kind of thing a flat generated logo can neither satisfy nor be checked for.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, the tonal and temperature set, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, remove_background in both the transparent and backgroundColor forms, crop_to_bounds and crop_and_resize with their tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor are all verified headless across 27 live calls, and alpha survives crops at outputFileType png so the platform tiles are real. The clipped specular checkpoint rests on the fact that the family offers no measurement of any kind, no eyedropper, no histogram and no hex readout, so whether a range still carries information is only observable as a change or the absence of one in the returned image, inspected through asset_inline_preview. No generative expand is used anywhere, so no plate edge is invented. image_vectorize is verified live as a headless trace that accepts NO options at all, so all tuning of whether the recovered mark's serifs and shell lines survive lives in the raster preparation; a compound mark selection is a verified finding to silently drop elements, naming the substrate returns the substrate, the trace emits no viewBox, and path index zero is always an opaque full canvas rectangle, which is why the recovery is worded to the engraving, the oyster device is taken on its own, and the viewBox is injected and the opaque ground path stripped by hand. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt as readout and validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout to a single press PDF with one record per page in verified row order, and document_render_layout at real resolution are all verified end to end and synchronous, with page count equal to row count confirmed as a checkable gate. Frame granularity from a PDF is documented as not controllable and as collapsing a continuous flow into a single frame, which is why the inventory is read before any mapping is promised, and the lossy structure readout with its silently short offsets is a verified live finding, which is why offsets are computed from the reconstructed story and placeholders confirmed by re-export. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, the product is a genuine editable dcx findable by asset_search, external image URLs render as empty grey boxes so plates are base64 inlined, inline SVG is verified to become native editable vector shapes so the recovered house mark stays editable rather than a flattened picture, mix-blend-mode is verified DROPPED with the element rendering as a plain opaque shape, backdrop-filter is verified dropped to its underlying flat fill, and the rendition preview is documented as page one only, which is why verification splits between rendition and returned markup. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB inline threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end including a browser proving licensed faces load; the case sensitivity, all or nothing kit and non standard numeric weight traps are all live findings. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returned a real 7360x4912 JPEG, boards persist with a hard cap of 12 placements per call and 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio (the entire family is unretrievable headlessly), no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no bleed gate, no pdfPreset, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text to image, no generative expand, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above 20 (13 plates).
